title: Simultaneous Ocular and Cervical VEMP Recording Protocol
author: Tatiana Rocha Silva
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zmzf476
materials: This protocol uses the Labat® equipment, two channels, connected to a laptop. (Figure 1 and 2). Figure 1. The laptop connected to Labat® equipment Figure 2. Tracing of ocular and cervical VEMP using Labat® equipment

steps.title: Position Electrodes
steps.instruction: Place electrodes for simultaneous ocular and cervical VEMP recording using two channels and a ground.

substeps.instruction: Place the ground electrode on the forehead.

For cervical VEMP (Channel 2): Place the active electrode at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle in its upper third on the opposite side of the stimulated ear, and the reference electrode in the sternal notch region.
For ocular VEMP (Channel 1): Place the active (negative) electrode approximately 1 cm below the lower eyelid, and the reference (positive) electrode approximately 1 cm from the active electrode.

steps.title: Position Participant
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to maintain specific head and eye positions during recording.

substeps.instruction: Have the participant sit in a chair with their head rotated to the opposite side of the stimulated ear to contract the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
Instruct the participant to look at a stationary target on the wall in front of them, then immediately look at a fixed point located approximately 30º above the horizontal plane.

steps.title: Configure Stimuli and Equipment
steps.instruction: Set up the auditory stimuli and recording parameters using ER 3A insertion phones with disposable foam eartips.

substeps.instruction: Set tone burst stimuli to an intensity of 120 dB nHL.
Apply a bandpass filter from 10 Hz to 1500 Hz.
Set the stimulus frequency to 500 Hz.
Set the stimulus rate to four stimuli per second.
Configure the scan window to 50 ms.

steps.title: Perform Recording
steps.instruction: Execute the VEMP recording and verify signal replication.

substeps.instruction: Check that impedance values are below 5 kΩ before each record.
Present 100 stimuli to obtain each record.
Perform at least two stimulations per side to verify replication of the potential.
